title: introduce-heuristic-release-annotator-and-profile-curation-workflow
author: Sasha Nguyen
release_notes: Adds a heuristic release annotator and profile curation workflow: generates concise changelog blurbs from profile deltas, tags variant provenance anchors, and exposes CLI flags for deterministic profiling seeds. Backwards compatible; opt-in via onboarding config.
body:
Summary: This PR adds a lightweight heuristic release annotator plus an associated profile curation workflow to help automate changelog blurbs and surface actionable profile deltas during model onboarding. The annotator synthesizes short, structured release notes from differences between successive model profiles (performance, latency distributions, and qualitative eval metrics), and attaches provenance anchors so downstream releases can be traced back to source artifacts.

Motivation: The registry holds many onboarding artifacts but developers still write release notes manually. We want consistent, machine-assisted release summaries that highlight material changes (perf regressions, size/quantization changes, new tokenization artifacts) and suggest rollout guidance.

Goals:
- Produce concise 1-3 sentence changelog blurbs per variant.
- Surface top 3 metric deltas with suggested actions (e.g., "consider enabling cache", "promote quantized candidate for cost-sensitive routes").
- Stamp provenance anchors (profile-hash, fingerprint, dataset-seed) so releases are auditable.
- Keep onboarding optional and incremental: users opt-in via onboarding config or CLI flag.

Implementation details:
- annotator/engine: Python microservice integrated into the onboard pipeline (registry/onboard/annotator.py). It consumes two profile JSONs (baseline, candidate) and produces an annotation object serialized as a compact blurb and list of gist-like notes. Heuristics include weighted scoring across metrics: latency p95, mean tokens/sec, normalized quality delta (we use the existing eval harness scores), model size (MB), and quantization flag. Each metric is assigned a tunable weight with defaults chosen from historical onboarding deltas.
- provenance anchors: we generate a deterministic fingerprint using model hash + dataset-seed + profiler-version (new CLI flag --profiling-seed). The fingerprint is stored in profile metadata as anchor:v1:<hex>.
- blurb synthesis: short sentences built from templated fragments with a beam of variants; we score candidates by clarity and conciseness heuristics and pick the top-ranked blurb. Example output: "Candidate variant 't1-7b-q4' reduces endpoint cost by ~28% (est.) with a 4% mean quality delta on deveval; recommend canary with caching enabled."
- profile curation workflow: a new workflow in registry/pipelines/curation.yaml that runs annotator, produces a curated_release.json, and pushes an automated change-note draft to Linear when configured.
- CLI: onboard-cli gains flags --profiling-seed and --annotate-release (boolean) to produce deterministic anchors and automatic drafts.
- Safety heuristics: annotations include conservative gating rules: if quality delta < -2% or latency regressions > 30% we mark annotation as "requires-review" and do not auto-post.

Tests and CI:
- Unit tests added for metric weighting and blurb templates (tests/test_annotator.py).
- Integration test that runs a small candidate/baseline pair and asserts the annotated gist matches golden fixtures (tests/fixtures/*).
- CI initially failed lint on a docstring; fixed and reran. All checks now green.

Review thread summary:
- Ava: requested stronger justification for default metric weights and asked for a way to override via org config. Response: added registry/config/annotator_defaults.toml and docs in redwood-model-registry/docs/annotator.md describing weight overrides per-tenant.
- Diego: asked to avoid auto-posting to Linear by default. Response: changed default to opt-out and added clear consent checks; documented the behavior.
- Emily: requested an audit log entry for every generated blurb. Response: added audit emit in the pipeline and a short retention note in docs.

Commits:
- c1a4f2d: add annotator core, blurb templates and scoring harness
- b9e7d3a: introduce provenance fingerprint generator and CLI flag --profiling-seed
- 4f2b6e1: pipeline: add curation workflow and Linear draft hook (opt-in)
- 77d9a11: tests and fixtures for annotator; golden fixture updates
- 8bb3e4c: docs, config defaults, and audit log emit
- faf5b12: fix linting and CI flakes

Changed files (high level):
- registry/onboard/annotator.py (new)
- registry/cli/onboard.py (CLI flags)
- registry/pipelines/curation.yaml (workflow)
- registry/config/annotator_defaults.toml (defaults)
- registry/docs/annotator.md (doc)
- tests/test_annotator.py, tests/fixtures/*
- registry/hooks/linear_draft.py (opt-in hook)

Rollout plan:
- Stage 1 (canary): enable annotator for internal onboarding only; keep Linear hook off.
- Stage 2 (customer opt-in): surface annotator in the Console onboarding flow and allow org-level defaults.
- Stage 3 (optional auto-post): allow teams to opt into automatic Linear drafts.

Migration notes:
- No breaking changes. Profiles gain two optional fields: provenance_anchor and curated_blurb. Existing tooling ignores them if absent.
- For deterministic fingerprints, teams should pass --profiling-seed or set a value in onboarding config.

Observability & monitoring:
- Added metrics: annotator.calls, annotator.duration_ms, annotator.decisions.* (counts of "auto-post", "requires-review").
- Added an alert (low volume after rollout) to detect if annotation success drops below 90%.

Security & privacy:
- The annotator never uploads raw datasets; it consumes aggregated profile metrics only. The Linear hook only posts draft text and the provenance anchor; secrets are masked.

Why this is different: prior PRs focused on changelog extraction from release streams or heavy-weight curated bundles. This PR intentionally targets the onboarding path, produces compact, actionable blurbs, and is designed to be conservative and opt-in.

Future work:
- Integrate with release note composer in Console to allow editing generated blurbs.
- Add a model-specific learned scoring model (replace heuristics) once we collect 1000+ annotated deltas.

Merge outcome: squash merge to main after approvals from Ava and Diego. Changelog automated entry created in CHANGELOG-curation.md.
review_comments: Ava Patel: Can we expose the metric weights per-org? Some teams weight latency much higher than quality.
Sasha Nguyen: Added annotator_defaults.toml and docs; weights are overridable via org config and Console settings (docs updated).
Diego Ramirez: Do NOT auto-post to Linear by default. We need explicit consent.
Sasha Nguyen: Switched Linear hook to opt-in; default remains off and pipeline will only create local draft files unless configured.
Emily Chen: Add an audit log entry when a blurb is generated so SRE/Compliance can trace back communications.
Sasha Nguyen: Added registry/audit emit path and a short retention policy note in docs.
